key_insight: A Bayesian inverse-game framework that infers other agents' objectives from high-dimensional, multi‑modal observations and produces calibrated uncertainty over hypotheses, enabling robust reasoning about strategic behavior.
problem_solved: Existing inverse-game approaches rely on maximum-likelihood estimation and break down with high-dimensional, multi-modal sensor data (images, trajectories, language) and complex strategic coupling; this work provides a scalable, uncertainty-aware solution for recovering objectives from such observations.
method: Formulate inverse games probabilistically: place priors on agent objectives and compute a posterior using a game-theoretic forward model as the likelihood.

Scale inference to high-dimensional, multi‑modal data by combining learned perceptual encoders (e.g., latent representations) with scalable Bayesian inference (amortized/variational inference or MCMC over surrogate differentiable game solvers).
Produce calibrated posterior samples over objectives for downstream planners and evaluate on multi-agent scenarios to demonstrate robustness and uncertainty quantification.
impact: Practitioners can infer other agents' goals from complex sensor streams while quantifying uncertainty, improving safety and decision-making in multi-agent systems (e.g., autonomous driving, robotics, multi-robot coordination).
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: multi-modal sensors (image, trajectory, text) -> encoders -> Bayesian inverse-game module -> posterior over objectives -> planner
Schematic game/utility diagram overlaid with a posterior heatmap to show uncertainty in inferred objectives
Latent-space visualization showing how multi-modal observations map to objective hypotheses (clusters/samples)
Performance and calibration charts: accuracy vs. observation complexity and posterior coverage/uncertainty plots
paper_title: Bayesian Inverse Games with High-Dimensional Multi-Modal Observations
paper_authors: Yash Jain, Xinjie Liu, Lasse Peters, David Fridovich-Keil, Ufuk Topcu
